t.zh: 检验条例用来检查声明是否符合我们想表达的意思。每条条例描述一种情况：有哪些前提、要推导什么目标，以及在这些前提下，目标预期能否推导出来。
t.en: A test case checks whether a declaration captures the intended meaning. Each case describes a situation: the available premises, the goal, and whether the goal is expected to follow from those premises.

t.zh: 声明规定了哪些推导可以成立。运行检验时，证明器会按声明给出结果，再与条例中的预期比较。结果不符，就说明声明在这种情况下没有表达出我们想要的意思。
t.en: A declaration specifies which derivations are allowed. When a test runs, the prover gives a result according to the declaration and compares it with the expectation. A mismatch shows that the declaration does not capture the intended meaning in that situation.

t.zh: 本关先为自己写的声明编写一条结果相符的条例，再为另一份声明找一条结果不符的条例，最后从两个方向检验同一份声明。
t.en: In this level, first write a case that agrees with your own declaration, then find a case that disagrees with another declaration, and last check one declaration in two directions.

after.zh: 检验条例只能找出声明的错误，证明不了声明正确。
after.en: Test cases can show a declaration wrong; they cannot show it right.

t.zh: 表上是你在<level-ref to="decl-and"></level-ref>写的声明。找出一种情况，使这份声明的结果与预期相符，并将这个情况填入表内。
t.en: The table holds your declaration from <level-ref to="decl-and"></level-ref>. Find a situation in which its result agrees with your expectation, and enter it in the table.

brief.zh: 需求：「下雨并且刮风」只在「下雨」和「刮风」都已证出时才能引入。找出一种情况：预期符合需求，声明的结果与预期相符。
brief.en: Requirement: “it rains and it is windy” may be introduced only when “it rains” and “it is windy” are both proved. Find a situation where the expectation meets the requirement and the declaration’s result agrees with it.

hint.zh: 先定下前提和目标，再按需求想：这时目标该不该推得出？
hint.en: Choose the premises and the goal first, then ask what the requirement says: should the goal be derivable?

t.zh: 表上换成了别人写的声明。找出一种情况，使这份声明的结果与预期不符，并将这个情况填入表内。
t.en: The table now holds someone else’s declaration. Find a situation in which its result disagrees with your expectation, and enter it in the table.

brief.zh: 需求：「下雨并且刮风」只在「下雨」和「刮风」都已证出时才能引入。找出一种情况：预期符合需求，声明的结果却与预期不符。
brief.en: Requirement: “it rains and it is windy” may be introduced only when “it rains” and “it is windy” are both proved. Find a situation where the expectation meets the requirement but the declaration’s result disagrees with it.

hint.zh: 这份声明要的前提和需求一样吗？
hint.en: Does this declaration ask for the same premises as the requirement?

t.zh: 检验一份声明，要从两个方向入手。引入方向以声明的命题为目标，检验在什么前提下可以得到它；使用方向把它放进前提，检验有了它之后能推出什么。引入规则决定前一个方向，由引入规则生成的消去规则决定后一个方向。
t.en: A declaration is checked from two directions. The introduction direction takes the declared statement as the goal and checks under which premises it can be obtained; the use direction puts it among the premises and checks what follows from it. The intro rules decide the first direction; the elimination rule generated from them decides the second.

t.zh: 表上的声明多了一条引入规则：有了「下雨 ∧ 刮风」，就引入「下雨 ∧ 刮风」。第 1 条条例已经写好，它从引入方向检验：结果与预期相符。事实上，从这个方向写出的任何条例，这份声明都能通过。
t.en: The declaration on the table has one intro rule too many: from “it rains ∧ it is windy”, introduce “it rains ∧ it is windy”. Case 1 is already written and checks the introduction direction: the result agrees with the expectation. In fact this declaration passes every case written from this direction.

brief.zh: 需求：「下雨并且刮风」只在「下雨」和「刮风」都已证出时才能引入。补全第 2 条条例，从使用方向找出这份声明的错误。
brief.en: Requirement: “it rains and it is windy” may be introduced only when “it rains” and “it is windy” are both proved. Complete case 2 to reveal this declaration’s fault from the use direction.

hint.zh: 这份声明的消去规则有两种情况。第二种情况从「下雨 ∧ 刮风」交还什么？
hint.en: This declaration’s elimination rule has two cases. What does the second give back from “it rains ∧ it is windy”?

hint.zh: 按需求，单凭「下雨 ∧ 刮风」，能推出什么？
hint.en: By the requirement, what follows from “it rains ∧ it is windy” alone?

after.zh: 只从引入方向检验，这份声明找不出错误：有了「下雨 ∧ 刮风」，「下雨 ∧ 刮风」当然成立。但多出的那条规则让消去规则多了一种情况，它什么都不交还，于是单凭「下雨 ∧ 刮风」再也推不出「下雨」。多写一条看似无害的引入规则，问题可能只在使用时暴露，所以两个方向都要检验。
after.en: From the introduction direction alone this declaration shows no fault: with “it rains ∧ it is windy”, “it rains ∧ it is windy” of course holds. But the extra rule gives the elimination rule one more case, which hands back nothing, so “it rains ∧ it is windy” alone no longer yields “it rains”. One harmless-looking extra intro rule may show its fault only in use, so both directions must be checked.
